newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: MAS maintains 5-7 pct Singapore growth forecast.
newsitem.headline: MAS maintains 5-7 pct Singapore growth forecast.

text.p: Singapore's economy is expected to grow by five to seven percent in 1997, the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) said in its 1996/1997 annual report on Tuesday.
The forecast is in line with the government's previous predictions.
The growth would be led by a recovery in manufacturing exports, continuing strong construction activity and a buoyant financial sector, it said.

"The turnaround in global electronics demand portends a recovery in Singapore's manufacturing sector in 1997," MAS said. It said that within the electronics industry the disk drive segment was expected to remain strong on continued firm demand and capacity increases in the pipeline.
Transport and communications along with the commerce sectors would in turn benefit from the improvement in manufacturing.

MAS said the construction sector in 1997 would be supported by a strong pipeline of projects in public works and non-residential buildings. But its growth was likely to taper off towards 1998 as projects were completed.
It said growth of domestic banking activity would be weaker, reflecting the impact on loan demand of the property market measures implemented in May 1996.
However, Asian Dollar Market activity was expected to strengthen, underpinned by strong expansion in offshore interbank and non-bank activity.
